Hello, am I speaking with Mr. Imran Nair? 

Good day, Mr. Nair. My name is Asha, calling from Meridian Receivables on behalf of Meridian Receivables. I'm calling regarding invoice INV-2026-1028 for Tulsi Packaging Pvt Ltd. 

I see that out of the total amount of ₹1,27,558, a partial payment of ₹34,458 was made, leaving an outstanding balance of ₹93,100 which was due on October 19th, making it 14 days overdue. 

I'm calling to see how we can arrange for the payment of this remaining balance today.

turns.speaker: debtor
turns.text: Haan, Imran Nair bol raha hoon. Dekhiye, ek sath 93,100 rupees dena abhi mushkil hai, kya hum isko installments mein de sakte hain?

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text:
Mr. Nair, I completely understand that paying the full remaining balance of ₹93,100 at once might be difficult right now. We can certainly arrange an installment plan for you. 

According to our company policy, we can split the balance into a maximum of 3 parts, with the final payment to be completed within 60 days. 

How would you like to structure these installments? For instance, what amount would you be comfortable paying in the first installment, and when can we schedule it?

args.query: installment plan policy maximum duration number of parts minimum down payment

results.text: An installment plan is allowed only when the outstanding amount is above INR 20,000. The outstanding amount is the invoice amount minus the amount already paid. A plan has at most 3 parts, the parts must add up exactly to the outstanding amount, and the last part must fall within 60 days of the call. If the outstanding amount is INR 20,000 or less, ask for full payment on a specific date instead. Log the agreed plan with the dates and amounts of every part.

If the debtor says they already paid, ask for the UTR number, the payment date and the amount. Log the payment claim with these details. Do not ask for payment again on this call. Tell the debtor the payment will be checked and that someone will follow up.

turns.speaker: debtor
turns.text: Theek hai, main first installment 30,000 rupees ki de sakta hoon, aur ye main coming Friday, matlab 6th November ko transfer kar dunga.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text:
That sounds reasonable, Mr. Nair. The first installment of ₹30,000 on November 6th, 2026 is noted. 

The total outstanding balance is ₹93,100, so after this first payment, we have ₹63,100 remaining. How would you like to split the remaining ₹63,100 across the next one or two installments, keeping in mind that the final payment needs to be within 60 days (by early January 2027)?

If the outstanding amount is INR 20,000 or less, ask for full payment on a specific date instead. Log the agreed plan with the dates and amounts of every part.

A promise to pay the full amount must be for a date within 30 days of the call. If the debtor cannot pay in full within 30 days, offer an installment plan when the debtor is eligible under the Installment Rules. If not eligible, ask for the earliest date within 30 days and log it.

Both installments together add up to the exact outstanding balance of ₹93,100. 

Is there anything else I can assist you with today, Mr. Nair?
